{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>STANDARD BUYER'S NON-DISCLOSURE AND CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>The undersigned (the "Buyer") understands and acknowledges that STONY HILL BUSINESS BROKERS, LLC (the "Broker") has been retained, for an agreed upon commission, to represent </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>_________________________________________ </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>(“Seller”) in the sale of the Business. </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>Buyer understands and acknowledges the Broker is acting as the agent of the Seller and that Broker's primary duty is to represent the interests of the Seller.</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>In order to induce Broker and Seller to furnish information regarding the Business (the "Information") to Buyer for Buyer's evaluation and possible purchase of said Business and in consideration for Broker and Seller furnishing such information, Buyer understands, agrees, represents and warrants to Broker and Seller as follows:</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>1. The word "Buyer”, as used herein shall mean and include the undersigned individually, and any partnership, limited liability company, corporation, or any other business entity identified below.</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>2. The Information is of a proprietary and confidential nature, the disclosure of which to any other party could result in damages to the Seller and/or Business.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>(a) The Information furnished by Broker or Seller has not been publicly disclosed, has not been made available to Buyer by any party or source other than Broker or Seller and is being furnished only upon the terms and conditions contained in this Agreement;</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>(b) Buyer will not disclose the Information, in whole or in part, to any party other than persons within Buyer's organization, including independent advisers/consultants, who have a need to know such Information for purposes of evaluating or structuring the possible purchase of the Business. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>Buyer accepts full responsibility for full compliance with all provisions of this Agreement by such other persons;</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>(c) Buyer will not disclose, except to the extent required by law, to any parties other than the persons described in Paragraph 2(B) above that the Business is available for purchase or that evaluations, discussions or negotiations are taking place concerning a possible purchase;</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>(d) Buyer will not utilize, now or at any time in the future, any trade secret(s), as that term may be defined under statutory or common law, that is/are included in the furnished Information for any purpose other than evaluating the possible purchase of the Business, including, without limitation, not utilizing same in the conduct of Buyer's or any other party's present or future business(es);</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>(e) In addition to the prohibition against utilizing trade secret(s), Buyer will not utilize any other furnished information for any purpose other than evaluating the possible purchase of the Business; and</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>(f) If Buyer decides does not purchase the Business, Buyer will promptly return to Broker all Information previously furnished by Broker or Seller, including any and all reproductions of same, and further, shall destroy any and all analyses, compilations or other material that incorporates any part of said Information.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>3. Buyer will not contact the Seller or Seller's employees, customers, suppliers or agents other than Broker for any reason whatsoever without the prior written consent of the Broker. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>All contacts with the Seller or such other parties will be made through or by Broker unless otherwise agreed to by Broker, in writing. </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>Seller’s employees may not be aware of the sale of the Business and Buyer agrees not to disclose to Seller’s employees that the Business is for sale, nor identify that Buyer is a possible purchaser of the Business.</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>4. The Information furnished by Broker has been prepared by or is based upon representations of the Seller and Broker has made no independent investigation or verification of said Information. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>Broker makes no representation that the Information is accurate or complete. </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>Buyer hereby expressly releases and discharges Broker from any and all responsibility and/or liability in connection with the accuracy, completeness or any other aspects of the information and accepts sole and final responsibility for the evaluation of the Information and all other factors relating to the Business. </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>Buyer understands and acknowledges that it has been advised to engage attorneys, accountants and other advisors to complete due diligence on the Business offered for sale to verify that the Business is satisfactory. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>Buyer understands that the future success or failure of the Business is primarily dependent on the Buyer’s knowledge and efforts and is not dependent on the Business’s past volume of business or profitability.</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>5. The Information is subject to change or withdrawal without notice and the Business is being offered for sale subject to prior sale or the withdrawal of said offering without notice.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>6. Buyer will indemnify and hold harmless the Broker and Seller from any and all claims or actions arising from Buyer's acts or failures to act in pursuing the possible purchase of the Business, including, without limitation, reasonable attorney's fees and other expenses incurred by Broker and seller.</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>7. Buyer will not, for a period of three (3) years from the date hereof, enter into any agreement for the purchase of the Business, in whole or in part, or assist or promote any other party in so doing, unless such agreement to purchase provides for commission to be paid Broker, with the commission being defined as the amount agreed upon by Broker and Seller in the "Business Listing Contract”, “Engagement Agreement” or similar agreement between those parties. </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>If Buyer violates the foregoing provision, Buyer will be liable for and pay any commission that would have been due to Broker by Seller upon demand without any obligation on Broker's part to first exhaust any legal remedies against Seller.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>8. Buyer represents that Buyer has sufficient financial resources to complete the transaction for the asking price and terms set forth herein. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>Buyer agrees to provide, upon request by Broker or Seller, financial statements, credit references and other pertinent information evidencing such financial sufficiency.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>9. The performance and construction of this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>All sums due hereunder shall be payable at the office of the Broker in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>The parties agree to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in and for Bucks County, Pennsylvania to enforce the terms of this Agreement. </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>Claims for injunctive relief may be filed in any court with appropriate jurisdiction over the matter. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>All other claims must be arbitrated in accordance with section 11 below.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>10. This Agreement shall be binding upon the Buyer, Buyer's heirs, executors, successors, assigns, administrators or representatives. </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>If any provision of this Agreement shall be held to be invalid, void or unenforceable, the remainder of the provisions hereof shall remain in full force and effect and this Agreement shall be construed as if such invalid, void or unenforceable provision had not been contained herein.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>11. Any controversy between the parties arising out of the terms, obligations, covenants or conditions of this Agreement, shall be arbitrated in Bucks County, Pennsylvania on written request of one (1) party served on the other. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>Such arbitration shall be under the rules of the American Arbitration Association. </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>The arbitrator shall have no authority to change any provisions of this agreement; the arbitrator’s sole authority shall be to interpret or apply the provisions of this Agreement. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>The expenses of arbitration conducted pursuant to this paragraph shall be born by the parties in such proportion as the Arbitrator shall decide.</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>12. The terms and conditions of this Agreement shall also apply to any other business and/or property on which Broker has been retained to represent the owner(s) in the sale thereof and on which Broker or owner(s) has furnished information to Buyer. </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>Further, it shall not be necessary for Buyer to execute any additional agreement(s) to that effect and any terms and conditions of this Agreement that refer to the date hereof shall automatically be adjusted to reflect the date on which Broker or owner(s) initially furnished information to Buyer on such other business and/or property.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>13. The provisions hereof cannot be modified, amended, supplemented or rescinded without the written consent of Broker and this Agreement sets forth the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto.</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43>EXECUTED ON THIS ______ DAY OF </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>___________________, 201___.</SPAN 44>

guidance.inspection: Reconstruct each complete operative definition of protected information, including incorporated definitions, list introductions, alternatives, exclusions, and form or identification conditions. Explicit-identification Entailment requires every protected item to be identified by the disclosing party; reasonable-understanding, nature, circumstances, or automatic-inclusion alternatives oppose it. Merely naming a recipient or saying information was disclosed by a party is not identification. For technical-only scope, use the decision-bearing definitional chain: express business, financial, marketing, customer, personnel, operational, or similar subjects oppose the hypothesis, but generic breadth, form language, recitals, or unrelated definitions do not. Verbal-information Entailment requires express inclusion of oral or verbal communications, even when later identification or written confirmation is required; a written category silent about oral information is not opposing evidence. Preserve necessary preambles, all decision-bearing alternatives, and independently responsive definitions; reject nearby use, disclosure, return, and negotiation provisions.

guidance.inspection: For each issue locate an operative permission, exclusion, restriction, or reservation and verify actor, action, protected object, purpose, recipient class, polarity, and every condition. Independent development requires development or derivation without using, accessing, or referring to protected information; third-party acquisition requires receipt from another source with lawful provenance and no confidentiality duty. Do not substitute either exception, a similarity observation, or general competitive activity for the other. Employee and nonemployee sharing require an operative disclosure or access permission; retain incorporated class definitions, need-to-know and purpose limits, undertakings, consent, and responsibility terms. A definition or incidental actor mention alone is insufficient, while an exclusive employee-only permission can oppose nonemployee sharing. Limited use requires an operative restriction to the stated purpose; purpose-qualified copying or disclosure is not enough, and broader internal-business or residuals use is opposing evidence. No-licensing requires an express no-right, no-license, ownership, or reservation provision concerning protected information; access, evaluation, review, or limited use alone neither entails nor contradicts it. Preserve all independently responsive clauses and governing lead-ins; reject unrelated lexical matches.

guidance.inspection: Read every return, destruction, copying, retention, and survival provision in its complete clause structure. Return-or-destruction Entailment requires one operative duty connecting the recipient, protected material, mandatory disposition, and an end event; qualifying corpus events include termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, abandonment, ceasing interest, and an express transaction-effective or closing transition that itself triggers delivery of covered property. A request-only duty does not qualify, and a termination clause elsewhere cannot donate its trigger. Copy permission requires an affirmative necessary-purpose exception, copies required for authorized use, or acknowledged automatic copying. A prohibition subject only to possible consent or approval is opposing evidence, not permission. Post-return possession requires an express exception allowing specified material or copies to remain after the governing disposition duty, with applicable holder, purpose, access, duration, and continuing-confidentiality limits. A duty covering all material or copies without an exception is opposing evidence; physical persistence or unrelated residual knowledge is insufficient. Survival requires continuation of an identified obligation after an end event, not merely a termination right, retention exception, or accrued-remedies clause. Preserve triggers, alternatives, exceptions, preambles, cross-references, and every independently repeated responsive provision.

guidance.inspection: Inspect the complete document for four distinct operative controls. Agreement confidentiality covers the agreement or its existence or terms, or the existence, content, status, or terms of discussions or negotiations. A direct sentence deeming those subjects confidential is complete responsive evidence by itself; when coverage instead depends on a protected-information definition plus a general secrecy duty, retain both, while ordinary transaction references remain insufficient. Compelled-disclosure notice requires legal, regulatory, governmental, subpoena, court, or administrative compulsion to trigger notice, information, or consultation to the disclosing party; preserve timing, legal-permission qualifications, and protective-order mechanisms. Unauthorized-use notice or bare permission to disclose is not enough. Under the supplied corpus supervision, solicitation evidence includes operative personnel hiring or solicitation restrictions and independently operative proxy or vote-solicitation standstill provisions. Preserve their governing lead-ins, target classes, duration, consent conditions, exceptions, and independently repeated responsive items; headings, definitions, exceptions, and incidental uses of the word solicitation do not suffice. Reverse engineering requires an operative prohibition on reverse engineering, decompiling, or disassembling protected material; general secrecy, copying, product-use, or intellectual-property language is not equivalent. No located clause is never proof of whole-document absence.
